chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, who said: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Salih ibn Sa'id, from his father Sa'id al-Halwani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

While Isa (peace be upon him) was traveling, he passed by a village and found its people dead in the streets and houses. He said: 'Indeed, these people died in wrath; and if they had died in other than that, they would have been buried.'

His companions said: 'We wish you would inform us of their story.' It was said to him: 'Call them, O Spirit of Allah.' So he said: 'O people of the village!' A responder among them answered: 'At your service, O Spirit of Allah.'
He said: 'What is your condition and what is your story?' He said: 'We were in health in the morning and spent the night in al-Hawiya.'
He said: 'What is al-Hawiya?' He said: 'An ocean of fire, in it are mountains of fire.'
He said: 'And what brought you to what I see?' He said: 'The love of this world and the worship of the Taghut (idols/devils).'
He said: 'And how much was your love for this world?' He said: 'Like the love of a child for its mother; when she approaches, he rejoices, and when she turns away, he grieves.'
He said: 'And how much was your worship of the Taghut?' He said: 'When they commanded us, we obeyed them.'
He said: 'So how did you answer me while the others are silent?' He said: 'Because their mouths are bridled with bridles of fire, and upon them are angels, strong and mighty.'
And indeed, I was among them but was not one of them. When the punishment struck them, it struck me with them. So I am hanging by a hair, fearing that I will fall into the fire.'
Isa (peace be upon him) said to his companions: 'Sleeping on dry grass and eating a little barley bread is better while preserving the safety of one's religion.'

key_terms.الطَّاغُوت: Idols or Devils, entities worshipped besides God
key_terms.الْهَاوِيَة: The Abyss or Deep Pit, a place of punishment
key_terms.رُوحَ اللَّهِ: Spirit of Allah, a title for Isa (AS)

ai.seo_question: What is the cause of the people's punishment in the fire according to the narration of Isa (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Thawab al-Amal*, Prophet Isa (AS) encounters villagers resurrected to explain their punishment, attributing it to excessive love for the world and blind obedience to the *Taghut*. One individual describes hanging by a hair in fear of falling into the fire, illustrating the precarious state of those who compromise their faith for worldly gain. Shaykh al-Saduq uses this to emphasize that a simple life with religious integrity is superior to a compromised existence, a theme resonating with Shia teachings on *Zuhd* (asceticism) and *Tawhid* (monotheism).
